314.title: Narrow AI
314.subtitle: A system engineered or trained to perform one task or a bounded family of tasks, with no reliable ability to transfer that competence to tasks outside its design envelope.

315.title: AGI (economic replacement threshold)
315.subtitle: AI counts as general when it can perform most economically valuable work at or above the level of the humans currently paid to do it.

316.title: AGI (cognitive task parity)
316.subtitle: AI counts as general when it can perform essentially any cognitive task that a typical or expert human can perform, as measured by benchmarks and Turing-style tests.

317.title: AGI (autonomous R&D capability)
317.subtitle: AI counts as general, for takeoff purposes, when it can run the full research loop in AI and adjacent sciences without human input, at the level of a strong human research team.

318.title: Transformative AI (TAI)
318.subtitle: AI that precipitates a societal transition at least as large as the agricultural or industrial revolutions, regardless of how the systems work or whether they are general.

319.title: Artificial superintelligence (ASI)
319.subtitle: An intellect that greatly exceeds the cognitive performance of the best humans in virtually all domains of interest, including scientific creativity, general wisdom and social skill.

320.title: Recursive self-improvement (RSI)
320.subtitle: A process in which an AI system improves its own capabilities, and the improved system improves itself further, so that gains compound across iterations.

321.title: Intelligence explosion
321.subtitle: A runaway increase in machine intelligence produced by recursive self-improvement, in which each generation of AI designs a markedly better successor on a shrinking timescale.

322.title: Technological singularity
322.subtitle: A point in the future beyond which technological change, driven by greater-than-human intelligence, becomes so rapid that human affairs can no longer be predicted or understood in current terms.

323.title: Hard versus soft takeoff
323.subtitle: The disagreement over whether the transition from human-level AI to superintelligence takes months (hard, or fast) or years to decades (soft, or slow), and whether it is smooth or discontinuous.
